name: Stapleton postcoital prophylaxis
question: Does postcoital trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole prevent recurrent urinary tract infection compared with postcoital placebo in healthy young women?

design.population: Nonpregnant female university students with at least two culture-documented UTIs in the preceding 12 months and estimated intercourse fewer than 12 times per month.
design.description: Three-arm double-blind randomized trial; 27 women in the postcoital arms were analyzed after excluding entry infections. Median culture-documented UTIs in the prior year were 3 with postcoital trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole versus 4 with postcoital placebo (P=.02).
design.locator: Full text, Study Population, pp 703–704; Patient Characteristics, p 704

verdictNote: The report does not identify a prespecified endpoint or threshold; 27 postcoital-arm patients were analyzed.
takeaway: In nonpregnant young women with recurrent urinary tract infections, postcoital trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole reduced symptomatic recurrence versus postcoital placebo during 180 days: 2/16 versus 9/11 analyzed women developed infection (P=.0001).

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Stapleton A, Latham RH, Johnson C, et al. "Postcoital antimicrobial prophylaxis for recurrent urinary tract infection. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial." *JAMA.* 1990;264(6):703-706. doi:10.1001/jama.1990.03450060049027
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Efficacy of Prophylaxis, p 704

results.measure: Analyzed women with symptomatic UTI during 180-day prophylaxis (16 postcoital trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole; 11 postcoital placebo)
results.note: The paper reports no prespecified endpoint role, significance threshold, or confidence interval.
results.locator: Full text, Efficacy of Prophylaxis, p 704

results.measure: Symptomatic infections per patient-year during 180-day prophylaxis in the analyzed postcoital arms
results.locator: Full text, Efficacy of Prophylaxis, p 704
